confirmed_sources.name: CWC Kerala daily river discharge 1950-2000 (NWDP resource)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Downloaded: 23,703,774 bytes, 134,069 rows, 21 stations, 19,588 Periyar rows - all exact. NEELEESWARAM n=10,884 starting 1971; ARANGALI n=8,276 from 1978; VANDIPERIYAR n=428 (year 2000 only). Combined with the 2001-2025 file this gives Neeleeswaram 19,362 daily values spanning 1971-2025.

Per-year counts are 291 (1971) then 365/366 EVERY year 1972-2000 with no exception - this file is strictly one reading per day. The twice-daily pattern only begins in the 2001-2025 file. confirmed_sources.name: Kerala SW manual daily rainfall (NWDP resource, mislabelled 1991-2020)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Downloaded: 24,200,224 bytes, 151,429 rows - exact. Real year span is 2000-2020, NOT 1991 as the filename says. 2018 holds 8,435 station-days; IDUKKI district 7,462 rows; ERNAKULAM 366 - all exact. BOYCE ESTATE (9.56472, 76.91056) 2000-2020, 176 days in 2018; Vannapuram (9.93611, 76.46333) 2002-2020, 189 days in 2018. Neriyamangalam and Boothathankettu exist for 2011 only. Confirmed.
confirmed_sources.relevance: Moderate - useful gauge rainfall for SCS-CN antecedent moisture, but see the caveat before treating any of it as catchment rainfall.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - every number is exact, but the geographic interpretation is over-stated.
confirmed_sources.caveat: TWO corrections. (1) The sweep calls BOYCE ESTATE and Vannapuram 'long-record catchment stations'. They are Idukki DISTRICT stations, not Idukki reservoir CATCHMENT stations. BOYCE ESTATE is in Peerumade tehsil (9.565N) on the southern/western slope; Vannapuram is tagged Thodupuzha tehsil but its stored longitude 76.463E sits well west of Thodupuzha town (~76.72E), so its coordinate is itself suspect. Filtering the file to the actual Periyar headwater box (9.6-10.2N, 76.85-77.35E) yields only Vandanmedu (n=248) and Chinnar (n=168) - both short records. (2) The 'River column is garbage' warning is fully justified: the single most common river label on these Kerala stations is 'Brahmaputra' (27,735 rows), followed by Tapi, Luni and Narmada. Trust lat/lon and station name only.

confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes - the 472/228 split, the 1980-2020 span, the 19 forcings, the LSTM series and the GHI lineage are all confirmed in the abstract.
confirmed_sources.caveat: The paper's own TITLE says '228 catchments' while the abstract says 472 with 228 gauged - the sweep's framing is correct but be aware the two numbers mean different things. IMPORTANT UNVERIFIED POINT: I did NOT confirm that any Periyar or west-flowing Kerala catchment is actually among the 472. Check the station list before assuming AquaSync's basin is covered.

confirmed_sources.name: Mishra et al., 'The Kerala flood of 2018: combined impact of extreme rainfall and reservoir storage' (HESS Discussions preprint)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Preprint page and full PDF (1,301,376 bytes) both retrieved. confirmed_sources.relevance: Moderate - its real value is the pointer in the caveat, not its conclusions.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly - every content claim is verbatim correct, but the sweep omitted the single most important fact about this document.
confirmed_sources.caveat: STATUS PROBLEM the sweep did not report: the page states 'The manuscript was not accepted for further review after discussion.' This is a REJECTED preprint, not a published paper. Do not cite its >500-year return period as established - especially since the peer-reviewed Current Science paper says the PRB received a 145-YEAR return period rainfall, a large contradiction. USEFUL LEAD instead: the paper says it pulled storage for all seven major Kerala reservoirs from India-WRIS for 2007-2018, and reports Idukki at 92.5% of FRL on 8 Aug 2018 - which agrees with the CWC bulletin's 92% on 01-08-2018.

rejected.name: Global Reservoir Surface Area Dataset (GRSAD)
rejected.reason: Cannot be obtained, and would not help if it could. dataverse.tdl.org returns HTTP 202 with a ZERO-BYTE body to every non-browser client - the landing page, the DOI redirect target, and its own native API (/api/datasets/:persistentId) all return 202 with 0 bytes. So no file could be listed, sized or downloaded, and the sweep's description of its contents was never actually verified against the resource. I confirmed the dataset genuinely EXISTS via DataCite (10.18738/t8/df80wg, state 'findable', 'Global Reservoir Surface Area Dataset (GRSAD)', Gao Huilin & Zhao Gang, Texas Data Repository, 2019, described as 'time series of area values for 6817 global reservoirs ... generated from 1984 to 2015'), which does corroborate the 6,817-reservoir and 1984-2015 figures. But the record STOPS IN 2015, so it cannot inform the August 2018 event this sweep exists to reconstruct, and for surface area it is superseded by RAT-Kerala's TMS-OS series (2017-2025, Kerala-specific, downloadable in one curl).

verification_notes: METHOD: all 30 URLs curl-checked; 28 returned 200, two returned 202 (doi.org->figshare, which resolves fine via the figshare API, and dataverse.tdl.org, which does not). I went past status codes: I downloaded and parsed the three NWDP CSVs (87 MB), the four PDFs, the eight RAT CSVs, the IMD 2018 NetCDF and the GUARDIAN rating-curve workbook, and re-computed every headline number. The sweep is unusually accurate - byte counts matched to the byte on all eight files where one was claimed (39,425,558 / 23,703,774 / 24,200,224 / 6,003,314 / 4,413,605 / 539,052 / 3,714,034 / 25,431,832). This is not a hallucinated list; the corrections below are refinements, not debunkings.

CORRECTION 1 - the flood peak WAS measured, just not at Neeleeswaram. The sweep's headline caveat says 'the peak was never measured'. That is true for NEELEESWARAM (18 of 31 August days; and the gap is worse than reported - 13 days missing: 5, 12, 16-22, 24-27, not the 7 claimed) and equally true for ARANGALI (missing 16-27). But VANDIPERIYAR, the upstream Periyar headwater gauge, recorded ALL 31 DAYS of August 2018 with no gaps, straight through the event: 15 Aug 223.7, 16 Aug 1023, 17 Aug 653.1, 18 Aug 202.6 m3/s. That is a continuous upstream boundary condition across the exact window AquaSync's flagship case study covers, and the sweep missed it entirely.

CORRECTION 2 - the 1950-2000 discharge file is one reading per day throughout. The sweep claims Neeleeswaram goes to '730/yr from 1978 as two readings per day'. Per-year counts are 291 (1971) then 365 or 366 for every single year 1972-2000. No year has 730. The twice-daily pattern (08:00 and 08:30, or 09:00/09:15) only appears in the 2001-2025 file.

CORRECTION 3 - district is not catchment. BOYCE ESTATE and Vannapuram are described as 'long-record catchment stations' inside the Idukki catchment. Both are in Idukki DISTRICT, not the Idukki reservoir catchment: BOYCE ESTATE is in Peerumade tehsil at 9.565N on the southern/western slope, and Vannapuram's stored longitude (76.463E) sits far west of Thodupuzha town (~76.72E), so its coordinate is itself doubtful. Filtering to the true Periyar headwater box leaves only Vandanmedu (248 days) and Chinnar (168 days), both short. There is effectively NO long rainfall record inside the Idukki catchment in this file.

CORRECTION 4 - a station coordinate conflict between two of the sweep's own sources. GUARDIAN places VANDIPERIYAR at (9.1525, 77.1525), across the border in Tamil Nadu; NWDP/CWC places it at (9.57333, 77.09056), the correct site of Vandiperiyar town in Kerala - a ~47 km discrepancy. NEELEESWARAM (10.18361, 76.49556) and ARANGALI (10.28611, 76.32222) agree EXACTLY between the two datasets, which isolates Vandiperiyar as the bad record. Use NWDP coordinates; if you apply GUARDIAN's Vandiperiyar rating curve, you are applying it to a gauge whose location that dataset has wrong.

CORRECTION 5 - the HESS preprint was REJECTED. Its page states 'The manuscript was not accepted for further review after discussion.' The sweep presents it as an 'open preprint' and repeats its >500-year return period finding without qualification. Worse, that figure directly contradicts the peer-reviewed Current Science paper in the same list, which says the Periyar basin received a 145-YEAR return period rainfall. Do not put the 500-year number in AquaSync-facing material. The preprint's genuinely useful content is its data trail: seven major Kerala reservoirs' storage from India-WRIS for 2007-2018, with Idukki at 92.5% of FRL on 8 Aug 2018 - which independently agrees with the CWC bulletin's 92% for 01-08-2018.

CORRECTION 6 - India-WRIS is unreachable, so the 'recovered API contract' is documentation, not access. The contract itself is transcribed faithfully (I verified all seven endpoints line by line in the repo source). But indiawris.gov.in (164.100.85.36) times out on TCP connect to :443 after ~21 s on every endpoint tried. The sweep reported '200' for the GitHub repo, which is correct but easy to misread as the API working. Retry from an Indian network before planning around it - this matters because WRIS is the route to the 2007-2018 storage series that the rejected preprint used.

SCOPE CORRECTION - the CWC bulletin archive starts in 2015, not earlier. Scraping pages 0-25 yielded 528 PDFs: 36 for 2015, ~50/yr for 2016-2024, and only one or two stray files per year for 2001-2012. So this gives weekly Idukki level+storage for 2015-2025 and nothing usable before that. The '45 of 52 for 2018' claim is exactly right - I enumerated the Thursdays and confirmed the 7 absentees (03-29, 05-10, 08-09, 08-16, 09-27, 10-18, 12-27), and I re-tested all 7 filename variants for the two flood weeks: 14/14 returned 404. The hole over the event is real.

TWO BONUSES the sweep under-sold. (1) The bulletins validate BOTH reservoirs, not just Idukki: the same PDFs carry '*81 IDAMALAYAR 169.00 167.03 1.018 0.961 01-08-2018 94 30 45 33 75', independently confirming AquaSync's Idamalayar FRL of 169.00 m and 75 MW alongside Idukki's 732.43 m / 1.460 BCM / 780 MW - four project constants cross-checked from one official PDF. (2) GHI does not merely 'mention the Periyar': it uses NEELEESWARAM ON THE PERIYAR as its worked example of CWC station location verification (Fig. 5), checking the official coordinate against the town 4 km west - published, independent QC of the exact gauge coordinate AquaSync routes to. Separately, the RAT dashboard exposes far more than the two dams named: kakki, banasurasagar, mullaperiyar, pazhassi, neyyar and malampuzha all return 200. Mullaperiyar is the important one - Suresh et al. show it intercepts and re-regulates flow that would otherwise reach Idukki, a genuine structural gap in any model treating Idukki inflow as natural.

PRACTICAL WARNING for whoever ingests the papers: BOTH the Current Science and NTRS PDFs extract with SHIFTED TABLE COLUMNS. In Current Science Table 1 the dam names do not line up with their type/year/length/height values (one row loses its Type, another its name), so the '14 dams' count is approximate. In the NTRS manuscript Table 1 the Sl.No/reservoir-name column is offset by one row against the coordinate column - the values themselves are right (Idukki 9.845/76.968/60 km2, Idamalayaar 10.222/76.706/28.3 km2, confirmed by cross-referencing the River column) but a naive parser will mis-assign every row. Read both tables visually. By contrast the CWC bulletin rows and the CWC report's prose extract cleanly and can be parsed.
